title: Trains to Clacton
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Clacton Air Show. Greater Anglia runs a direct train from London Liverpool Street to Clacton-on-Sea every hour, and you can get there from its other main stations too, with a change at Colchester or Shenfield. If you’re starting on the c2c line, from Shoeburyness, Southend, Basildon, Grays or anywhere along to Barking, I’ve added those stations too, with the change in London. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Clacton Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: From the station it’s about 10 to 15 minutes on foot. Head down through the town centre to the seafront, then turn right for the West Greensward.
walkBack: Allow about 15 minutes to walk back up to the station from the West Greensward, and a bit more when the crowds leave.
legs: Out past Bethnal Green and through Stratford. You run alongside the Elizabeth line most of the way to Shenfield, so it’s one of the busiest bits of railway in the country.
This is where it opens out into the Essex countryside. Some trains stop at Ingatestone on the way, so check your train in the station list.
Past the new Beaulieu Park station and on through Witham. A few trains also call at Hatfield Peverel, Kelvedon and Marks Tey.
After Colchester the train leaves the main line, calls at Hythe and follows the River Colne down to Wivenhoe. Some trains stop at Alresford, Great Bentley and Weeley too.
Thorpe-le-Soken is where the line to Walton-on-the-Naze goes its own way. From here it’s the last few minutes down to Clacton, the end of the line.
tip: Trains are very busy straight after the flying, as everyone heads for the station at once. I would either leave a little early, or stay in town for something to eat and catch a later train.

In 2026 there was a twilight display on the Thursday evening, and I would check the 2027 programme to see if it returns. In the current timetable the last direct train to London leaves Clacton at 22:05, so I would check this before any twilight display starts.
Greater Anglia usually adds extra trains on airshow days, and the summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.
alt: When I last checked, an off-peak day return from London was £53.90, or £44.10 super off-peak on trains from about midday.
If you’re going as a family, a Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares. It may well pay for itself on this one trip.
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows train services run by Greater Anglia. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Thursday 5 and Friday 6 November 2026, checked on 30 October 2026. The big stations and city termini further from Clacton-on-Sea use the times for Friday 13 November 2026, checked on 10 November 2026. Times for summer 2027 usually come out in the spring, so please check with Greater Anglia before you travel. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. gaOnly: Greater Anglia trains only. Due to how complicated the rail network is, I only show train services run by Greater Anglia. Every journey here is Greater Anglia from start to finish, changes included. If you’re coming from further away, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there. I’ve also added eight c2c stations, with the c2c train into London and the connection on from there.
pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. They can sell out, so book as soon as the show dates are out.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.
Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off. Have a look at the one that fits you before you book.
faq: Which station is closest to the show?
Clacton-on-Sea. It’s the end of the line and about a 10 to 15 minute walk down through the town to the seafront and the West Greensward.

There was one on the Thursday evening in 2026, and the 2027 plans had not been confirmed when I last checked. In the current timetable the last direct train to London leaves Clacton at 22:05, so I would check the times before any twilight display starts.
Will there be extra trains on show days?
Greater Anglia usually adds extra trains on airshow days, and the summer 2027 times come out nearer the show, so please check before you travel.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
I’m coming from further away. What do I do?
I only show Greater Anglia trains on this page, so I would plan your trip to one of the eight stations here first and pick it up from there.
access: Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
Check the station has step free access to every platform you need, both ways.

x.tipArrive: I would try to arrive well before the flying starts. If you want a front row seat, head there first and save your pitch, then take a look round the static aircraft, speak to the crews, visit the trade stalls and check the food options. Visit the toilet before the flying display starts.
checks: Ear defenders packed for the children
